title: A planned three-trombone project
summary: He wants to write for three B-flat trombones playing slurs, marking positions, and would try Dicky Wells.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yeah, (inaudible). That's why I'm telling you that I want to do a trombone thing with about three

trombones and that will show everybody what can be really played with a trombone. A trombone is made for slurring and movements. Nobody's ever written nothing for it that way. Move a little bit and that's the end of it, little bit . But if you ever heard a brass band and you heard that trombone, (inaudible), those trombones start in that seven position and they in rhythm, they all the way up here.
Yeah.
And that's what made kids like trombones. They like that "aaaaaah," you know?
(Laughter.)
Yeah, that's right.
That's what attract the peoples' attention, but they don't do too much of it.
Do you -- well do you do your thing --
Stop.
Huh?
(Recording interruption.)
Well, what would you do with three or four trombones?
I would use three.
And what would they be?
I'd use three B-flat trombones -- don't
need the bass or nothing like that. Get any way (inaudible).
Yeah.

You know, it's too hard to play. I'd use three B-flat trombones, a tenor ________, which there used to be tenor trombones. They changed the B-flat, but they -- and here's the difference. Four trombones are great when you sustain it and not move it fast. You can hear it.
Yeah.
But three trombones moving can sound just as great as six sustaining and three can move easy. (Inaudible) because you got to use certain positions, certain keys.
Who would you use?
You don't let them break them slurs and that's all (inaudible). You got to know the horn and a musician ain't going to know that until I write it and then I marks the position.
Yeah.
Just like that. They say, 'Oh, I didn't know you could get that.' I say, 'Yeah, you got six different F's on that horn.' 'Well, I didn't know it. I knew two.'
(Laughter.)
You know?
Yes, --
You don't let them break for slur, just

like fiddles are better when they don't break, you know? Like fiddles are playing violin, and you play -- when you play the violin -- if you got three violins and one's got to come down and the other one's got a short long note and he got to go back up while they coming down, you can tell it.
Yeah, I see.
That's why they all got to pull the same way.
Yeah.
(Inaudible) all the time.
Who would you use for your three trombones today?
Would I use?
Yeah, which guys would you use?
I tell you one thing. Dicky Wells can play the music. He's one guy. He got a big tone and can play.
Oh, yeah.
And I don't know. I could probably break him on it. He would understand it.
Yeah.
Got to use somebody experienced, because he would know what you're after. Pick up quick. He's one guy in my -- get about five or six more and out all of them, you find somebody. Try out.
Yeah, I was wondering which guys
would sort of fit that trio best.
Yeah, before I hire them, I make them come in and test. See what happens, audition on the music (inaudible) do it.
Yeah, yeah.
But I hadn't thought about it. That's why you cut it down, you can get three. I know a couple of young white boys, too, that's got range.
